subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser navigation deny/warn policy for public URL/domain/path patterns, and what security contract should it expose?
rationale: This is a new operator-facing browser security/config surface, and the repository policy treats config additions and security boundaries as maintainer-sensitive rather than safe autonomous repair work.

options.title: Design Scoped Browser Policy
options.body: Approve a narrow browser-only deny/warn contract with explicit redirect, proxy, profile, and default-list semantics before implementation starts.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Track this under a broader cross-tool network policy with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685 so browser, web_fetch, and web_search do not grow conflicting controls.

options.title: Keep Current Host Exceptions
options.body: Decline a deny/warn surface for now and document `hostnameAllowlist`/`allowedHostnames` as the only supported browser navigation policy knobs.

recommendation.title: Design Scoped Browser Policy
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow browser-only deny/warn contract with explicit redirect, proxy, profile, and default-list semantics before implementation starts.

likelyOwner.reason: Their browser SSRF default and navigation-guard commits are the strongest history signal for the current security boundary.
